newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-MCCALL TO MEET LEWIS FOR WBC TITLE DESPITE TROUBLES.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-MCCALL TO MEET LEWIS FOR WBC TITLE DESPITE TROUBLES.

text.p: Troubled heavyweight Oliver McCall was unable to attend his own news conference Wednesday after another run-in with the law, but promoters are betting he will show up for his World Boxing Council title fight with Briton Lennox Lewis.
"Look he is fighting for the heavyweight championship of the world. He is fighting a guy who he knocked out the last time he fought and he's making $3 million.
"If he doesn't show up, he really should be committed," said Lewis promoter Dino Duva of McCall at a news conference to announce the February 7 bout in Nashville, Tennessee for the vacant WBC crown.
McCall was a no-show for the fight announcement in New York after being arrested in Nashville earlier this week on charges of vandalism, disorderly conduct and resisting arrest.
He was due to be arraigned on Thursday for the incident which began when he threw a Christmas tree in a hotel lobby.
So at the New York Hilton in a room filled with reporters, it was Lewis who asked the question of the hour: "Oliver McCall, where are you?"
"He took a misstep in the alcohol division, by that I mean he took a drink," offered McCall promoter Don King, who joined the proceedings via telephone hookup from Nashville.
"He's ok," insisted King of the fighter who also had a drug arrest earlier this year and has been in and out drug rehabiltation facilities over the last few years.
"He will be there to fight on February 7 and he will knock out Lennox Lewis," King promised.
The 28-6 McCall, who lost the WBC title to Frank Bruno 15 months ago, has not fought anyone but the police since March, when he stopped journeyman James Stanton in the sixth round.

The Nashville fight will be a chance for Lewis to avenge his lone defeat. Lewis, 29-1, lost his WBC crown to McCall when the American stopped him in the second round at Wembley Arena in September, 1994.
Lewis, who looked none too sharp in taking a 10-round decision from American Ray Mercer in his last outing in May, promised a different result this time around.
"He got through with a lucky punch," Lewis said of the right hand that floored him. "Nobody has beaten me twice and if Oliver McCall feels he can beat me again he is gravely mistaken."
Lewis's manager, Frank Maloney, suggested that McCall's drinking and arrest was part of his training strategy.
"You laugh, but the last time he fought Lennox his first four weeks training he was in rehab before he came across to England," Maloney said. "So he's just doing the same thing again."
Added Lewis: "All I have to say is if Oliver McCall beats me, then I definitely deserve to retire. It doesn't make sense to go on if Oliver McCll beats me."
